content.text:
This is a **BMW product decision support prototype**. It turns supplied customer feedback into draft requirements for future vehicles, shows the evidence behind each draft, calculates an exploratory priority range, and lets a product manager record a decision. The main demonstration focuses on **US feedback for the G60 5 Series**. F70 and G70 data are available for later transfer checks.

### What it does

1. The ingestion code reads the feedback and study workbooks. It keeps source hashes and spreadsheet locations, and treats repeated annotation rows for one feedback ID as **one feedback record**. See [feedback.py](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/src/bmw_pm/ingestion/feedback.py) and [studies.py](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/src/bmw_pm/ingestion/studies.py).
2. The extractor finds text about topics such as controls, software, charging, comfort, and driver assistance. The current stored run used a **keyword baseline**; an optional OpenAI extractor exists but requires credentials and a selected model. See [baseline.py](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/src/bmw_pm/intelligence/baseline.py) and [provider.py](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/src/bmw_pm/intelligence/provider.py).
3. The pipeline groups signals into customer outcome cards with supporting quotes, praise or preservation evidence, assumptions, and missing facts. See [pipeline.py](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/src/bmw_pm/pipeline.py) and [requirements.py](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/src/bmw_pm/intelligence/requirements.py).
4. Deterministic code scores each card under a visible, **unapproved equal-weight policy**. Missing inputs widen the score range instead of being guessed. The [Streamlit app](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/ui/app.py) displays the cards, evidence, score breakdown, uncertainty, and review history. Decisions and edits are stored as revisions with an audit trail.

### What is in the local database now

I inspected the SQLite database directly. It contains **10,128 feedback records** from 13,771 annotation rows, 391 study observations, 2,518 extracted signals, and **seven draft requirement cards**: comfort, controls, storage, driver assistance, software reliability, cabin noise, and charging/range. There are **no recorded PM decisions**. All seven cards remain `needs_review`.

Only feedback recurrence supplies a numeric scoring input in the current run. The other value criteria and engineering feasibility are unresolved, so **all 21 comparisons between the seven cards have overlapping ranges**. The displayed order is exploratory, not a recommendation to build one feature first.

### Other parts and current limits

- A separate [YouTube research tool](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/youtube_research_agent/README.md) can search videos, inspect transcripts, and review timestamped findings. It is **not integrated into the decision scores**. Its saved local probe has zero discovered videos and zero findings.
- A [120-record evaluation set](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/docs/EVALUATION_LABELING.md) has been frozen, but all 120 human-label entries are still unlabelled. Extraction accuracy and ranking quality therefore have **not been measured**.
- [Docker/Render hosting](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/docs/HOSTING.md) and a private database snapshot are prepared; the documentation says the app has **not been deployed**.
- The working tree contains ongoing changes and an **unresolved Git index conflict** for `youtube_research_agent/agent.py`. Its working file has no conflict markers, but Git still lists it as unmerged.
- I made no file changes. I attempted the test suite, but this Python environment has no `pytest` or project dependencies installed, so I cannot claim a fresh test pass.

The best overview is [README.md](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/README.md); the most candid account of what remains unfinished is [internal/TASKS.md](C:/Users/firas/Desktop/bmw-hackathon/internal/TASKS.md).
